comparison: Perfect agreement. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers find the descriptive statistics about K99/R00 award numbers (C1, C2, C52, C57, C58) to be SUPPORTED. Both note these are straightforward data summaries from NIH Reporter without complex statistical analysis required.

Disagreement on gender classification methodology. OpenEval rates claims C3, C99-C103 as UNCERTAIN due to inherent biases in name-to-gender classification that cannot capture transgender, non-binary, or gender non-conforming individuals. Peer reviewers rate the same claims as SUPPORTED, explicitly stating 'limitations of the data and the name-gender matching algorithm are described satisfactorily.'

Partial overlap with agreement. Both address conversion rate data (C4, C37, C59-C60). OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED as straightforward proportions. Peer reviewers also accept these findings as SUPPORTED, though their result additionally covers gender-related claims that OpenEval evaluated separately.

Perfect agreement. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers find institutional concentration claims (C5-C6, C72-C85) to be SUPPORTED. Both note the clear institutional hierarchy and geographic concentration patterns are well-documented in the data and figures.

Partial overlap with agreement. Both address mobility-related claims (C61-C68). OpenEval finds conversion rate and mobility data SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers also accept these findings as SUPPORTED, highlighting the finding about researcher mobility's effect on funding success as 'key and novel.'

Partial overlap with agreement. Both address temporal trends in departmental mobility (C69-C70). OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED as straightforward descriptive findings. Peer reviewers also accept these patterns as SUPPORTED within their broader evaluation of mobility findings.

Agreement despite OpenEval caveat. Both find cumulative disadvantage claims (C7-C10, C113-C123) SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes appropriate Cox modeling but mentions gender classification limitations propagate uncertainty. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm these findings as a major contribution, describing them as empirically demonstrating persistent barriers.

Partial overlap with agreement. Both address hiring flow patterns. OpenEval finds claims C86-C98 SUPPORTED as straightforward proportions. Peer reviewers find overlapping claims C86-C91, C104-C112 SUPPORTED, describing the institutional hierarchy as echoing previous research on rigid faculty hiring networks.

Partial overlap with agreement. Both address institutional concentration metrics. OpenEval finds claims C104-C112 SUPPORTED with clearly defined classifications. Peer reviewers also find these claims SUPPORTED, noting they provide compelling evidence of inequalities in faculty funding opportunities.

Perfect agreement. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers find HBCU representation claims (C11, C126-C131) to be SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers explicitly highlight these findings as 'incredible facts' demanding attention, calling the distribution 'a massive oversight.'

Partial overlap with agreement. Both address Wapman dataset analysis. OpenEval finds claims C132-C142 SUPPORTED as straightforward descriptive statistics. Peer reviewers find overlapping claims plus C143-C156 and C184-C188 SUPPORTED, describing the HBCU faculty flow analysis as an important extension.

Partial overlap with agreement. Both address faculty hiring patterns from Wapman dataset. OpenEval finds claims C143-C156 SUPPORTED as descriptive statistics aligned with prior literature. Peer reviewers also find these claims SUPPORTED, noting they provide a more nuanced look at faculty pathways beyond high-status institutions.

Agreement on interpretive synthesis. Both find claims C162-C163 SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes valid inference from presented data about prestige aligning with NIH funding. Peer reviewers affirm these conclusions, noting alignment with Matthew effect and empirical demonstration of persistent barriers.

Perfect agreement. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers find racial disparity claims (C193-C197) from FOIA data SUPPORTED. Both note the specific data source and accept the documented disparities in K99 award rates and R00 transition rates.

Disagreement on speculative explanations. OpenEval rates claims C164-C169 as UNCERTAIN, noting they are explicitly speculative hypotheses without supporting data. Peer reviewers rate overlapping claims C166-C169 plus other speculative claims as SUPPORTED, accepting them as reasonable interpretations with policy implications.

Disagreement on speculative inferences. OpenEval rates claims C171, C173 as UNCERTAIN, noting they are explicitly speculative about downstream effects without supporting data. Peer reviewers include C173 in their SUPPORTED evaluation, accepting these as reasonable policy-relevant interpretations.

Disagreement on speculative explanations. OpenEval rates claims C176-C178, C180-C181 as UNCERTAIN, noting lack of data on unfunded applications prevents testing these hypotheses. Peer reviewers rate these same claims as SUPPORTED, accepting them as reasonable interpretations despite acknowledged data limitations.

Disagreement on policy recommendations. OpenEval rates claims C189, C191-C192 as UNCERTAIN, noting they are explicitly speculative hypotheses and policy recommendations rather than demonstrated findings. Peer reviewers rate these claims as SUPPORTED, accepting them as having important policy implications.

Disagreement on recommendations. OpenEval rates claims C201-C205 as UNCERTAIN, noting recommendations are logical but not empirically tested. Peer reviewers include overlapping claims C203-C205 in their SUPPORTED evaluation, accepting them as reasonable policy implications from the findings.

Agreement on limitations. Both find limitation claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes C198-C200 accurately describe study limitations verifiable from Methods. Peer reviewers find overlapping claims C198-C200 plus C174 adequately described, explicitly acknowledging data availability constraints are not the authors' fault.

OpenEval evaluated claims C54-C56, C175 about K99 awardees who did not transition to R00 as SUPPORTED, noting straightforward counts with logical temporal cutoff reasoning. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims.
